what_its_for: Isocarboxazid is used to treat depression, especially when other antidepressants have not worked. It belongs to a class of medicines called monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), which help improve your mood by increasing certain natural chemicals in your brain.
how_to_take: Take isocarboxazid by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Do not crush or chew the tablets. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too quickly may cause problems.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg twice a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to a maximum of 60 mg per day depending on how you respond to the medicine. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store isocarboxazid at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: This medicine has very important food and drug interactions that can be life-threatening. AVOID foods high in tyramine, including aged cheeses (like cheddar, brie, and blue cheese), cured or smoked meats, fermented foods, soy products, fava beans, tap beer, red wine, and overripe or pickled foods. AVOID alcohol completely. Do not take other antidepressants (including SSRIs like fluoxetine or sertraline, SNRIs, tricyclics, or other MAOIs), stimulants, decongestants (like pseudoephedrine), certain pain medicines (like meperidine/Demerol), or St. John's Wort within 14 days of using this medicine. Tell ALL of your doctors and pharmacists that you take this medicine before starting any new medication, including over-the-counter medicines. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or drowsiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a sudden severe headache, stiff neck, fast or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, nausea, vomiting, sweating, or vision changes — these could be signs of a dangerous rise in blood pressure called a hypertensive crisis. Also contact your doctor if you notice worsening depression, new or increased thoughts of suicide or self-harm, unusual agitation or restlessness, confusion, high fever, severe muscle stiffness, fainting, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Seek emergency help immediately if you think you are having a medical emergency.
when_it_works: Isocarboxazid may take 2 to 4 weeks before you start to feel better, and sometimes up to 6 to 8 weeks for the full benefit. Do not stop taking it even if you do not feel improvement right away. Keep taking it as directed and talk to your doctor if you have concerns about how it is working.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and falls, so extra caution is needed. This medicine is NOT recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding due to potential harm to the baby. It is not approved for use in children or teenagers under 16 years of age. If you have liver disease, kidney problems, heart disease, high blood pressure, a history of seizures, or are planning surgery, tell your doctor before taking this medicine. Always give your full medical history to your healthcare provider.
